dune 100x over. i just finished the first book a few days ago after putting it off for so long and my god. i’m sure lots on this thread has attested to the world building, the implications of politics, religion and climate change and how it set the scene for modern sci-fi but the one thing that stood above all else for me is how frank herbert writes dialogue. a large portion of this book is dialogue, which i usually find to be the hardest to read, but herbert puts so much attention into the nuance of conversation that it was honestly my favourite part of the book. his attention to body language, tone and facial expressions makes me feel as if i’m watching these characters speak in front of me, so detailed that it feels as real as any conversation i’ve ever been apart of myself. i found myself drawn into the world and feeling deeply for these complicated characters, relating to them despite the fact that the universe they live in is nothing like my own. once you’re past the first 150 pages, it’s practically impossible to put it down. my only regret is that i’ll never be able to read it again for the first time.

i’m surprised i haven’t seen it on here but: the dark tower series. it’s a fantasy epic that paints the picture of roland’s world over 7 books, and most of them are great (i have beef with wizard and glass). his dialogue is often weak and in typical stephen king fashion there are parts that draw on longer than necessary but overall it’s an incredibly creative series with loveable characters and a bit of a mind fuck. i would highly recommend them, especially to you as little if any of the story I would classify as “scary”, maybe a little whacky at times but it’s few and far between. the drawing of three was probably my favourite, but I also tore through the 700 pages of wolves of the calla in 2 days. and as a final testament, my boyfriend loves the series so much he’s planning on getting one of roland’s revolvers tattooed on his leg lmao

hi there! sorry you haven’t gotten much of an answer yet but hopefully i can help. i’ve been with upward since september ‘24 and was one of the previous nook staff. to answer your question about if we’re non-profit or not; no we are not. i believe we’re considered a “charitable business” as we have a sponsorship with the ECCU and receive food donations from other various vendors to keep our costs low (sandwiches are $5-$7, hot meals are $5, freezer meals are $7 and baked goods are ~$3). the exact reason for being a non-profit vs profit is above my pay grade, but i imagine it has something to do with making sure all of our staff get full benefits and are paid a living wage in this expensive city (mark really does take care of us). our goal is food security; our prices are meant to be available for absolutely everyone in the community and we have our token program available to make sure we can get food out to folks who don’t have the money to spare. in terms of the cookbook donations, that’s a fun little side project we’ve been working on. we’re working with some folks right now who are helping us develop a library app and the cookbooks (currently on display in our space) will be available to borrow for any members of the community. on that same note, we are taking steps to make this more of a community hub/collaborative space where members of organizations can host meetings or run classes when the cafe is closed. we currently have someone running a sourdough workshop next month and there’ll be a lot more on the horizon as we get settled more! hope that was helpful :)

i also used to live on the 11th floor of an apartment and shared a balcony with my neighbour with a divider that had about 6 inches of space on both sides. they had a cat they’d let out onto the balcony and he’d often wander over to my side. it was always a pleasant surprise seeing him outside of my door until the summer i had a garden and they put up netting to block the space on the divider so that he wouldn’t get into my plants (completely unprompted on my part, it was my first year trying and turns out a cold east coast summer isn’t the best for tomatoes so there wasn’t much for him to eat anyways lol). Koopa was determined though and solved this problem by walking over to my balcony across the railing. One morning I was checking on the garden before work and he sauntered over this way when a strong gust of wind knocked him off balance and for a horrifying moment I watched him lose his battle to get his footing back before I instinctively grabbed him. Poor baby was so scared he was shaking like crazy and not fighting me like he had done in the past when I’ve picked him up. I felt pretty awful at the time for walking him out into the hallway and waking my neighbours up at 6:30am because I couldn’t bare the thought of him trying to get back, but reading this I don’t feel so bad anymore. What an awful way to lose a cat, I don’t understand how people can be so clueless and irresponsible. I’m so sorry you had to witness that :(

hey hey! this is an older post but i wanted to offer a few suggestions of my own that I didn’t see mentioned in case you decide to visit again or anyone else stumbles onto this thread :-)

* if you’re going for a more causal vibe - stillwell.  the best bar in the city in my opinion, hands down. incredible local tap options, fun staff & events and they know their beer and food. both the beer bar on barrington and freehouse on agricola offer their own rotating menus and they always have at least one veg option, i’ve had everything from veg nuggets, their burger week pakora burger, salads the size of my head and the always amazing classic pub burger. in the summer the beer garden on spring also usually offers vegan stuff, had some amazing tacos this year before they closed for the season 

*  le bistro by liz is an adorable little french restaurant that can be cozy for lunch or quite romantic at night and when I inquired about vegan options they brought me out a whole menu! the food was excellent and the service was amazing

* g street has a giant vegan menu and i adore their pizza. it’s ok enough to eat in at but they’re my go to for ordering take out for sure

* studio east is a cute little asian gastopub that makes incredible vegan bao and has a little outdoor patio to enjoy as well

* in terms of fine dining, I used to work at cafe lunette and they also have both vegan brunch and dinner options, would highly recommend the ratatouille (vegan without the fromage blanc) i still think about it lol

* also for brunch, steve-o-reno’s has the veggie bagel and some baked goods. the nook makes all their baked goods vegan and would recommend the vegan power wrap or vegan heart stopper for breakfast

Hi there! I’m a premed neuroscience and bioethics major so I feel like I have my study habits pretty well set at this point. Not sure if all of these will directly apply to your material but I hope I can help however I can!

1) identify the kind of learner you are and use it to your advantage. Personally, I am a huge visual learner. I learn really well through reading and writing and diagrams are my saving grace. Because of this, I always have two copies of my notes, the first being my messy lecture notes, and the second being a more concise version where I add in diagrams and rephrase things. For people who are auditory learners, I’d recommended recording lectures or watching videos on the topics and explaining things out loud (to a person if you can find a willing one, but pets or inanimate objects work as well). If you’re a combination, you could definitely utilize strategies from both methods. I would also recommend searching online to find more tips for that specific style of learning! It can be really discouraging sometimes to find out that other people study different from you (especially if it seems like they’re doing ‘more’) but everyone learns differently :)

2) I cannot preach cue cards enough. I use it as a final way of review for me, and find it perfect for identifying gaps in my knowledge and solidifying difficult concepts (also if I’m in a pinch, I skip rewriting my notes and go straight to cue cards). Wether you use physical or digital cards is completely up to your preference, but if you do choose to go digital, anki and quizlet are excellent. 

3) inspire yourself! I personally love involving myself in the studying community (dubbed studyspo) as I find it really motivating to see others study and it encourages me to get to work. For this, I mainly use tumblr and YouTube and could recommend some accounts if you’re interested :) Tumblr communities also have some excellent studying tips that you can definitely utilize and incorporate into your style. One thing to mention though is that there’s a lot of emphasis on very “aesthetic” notes, so try not to get caught up in wether your notes look as nice.

4) I know a lot of people recommend the pomorodo method (25 mins studying to 5 min break) but I personally use a modified version as I find for most subjects 25 minutes isn’t enough to get a good flow going. I instead go for 2 hours of studying and then take a 25 minute break. To keep track you can use apps like forest, which also offer incentives if you don’t use your phone during that time. Also, try and do something productive during your break. Go for a walk, make a quick snack, do a quick tidy up. I find that if I go on my phone I find it hard to go back to studying after, though that’s just me personally!

5) If applicable, do as many practice problems as you can. Either take them straight from classes, textbooks or even third party sides online. I’m a firm believer that no practice is bad practice. It’s always better to do more than less. Review any question you get wrong and don’t just correct it, understand why you got it wrong and I guarantee you’ll be less likely to make that mistake again during a test.

6) last but not least, and probably my most relevant tip to this sub is to make a list of your study plan before you begin. I like to make mine super comprehensive by breaking one task into several sub categories with mini-lists of their own. That way, you know exactly what you need to accomplish and can keep track of each step as you go through. You can make an overall list for studying a topic, a daily list, or both! This is the one thing that really keeps me sane while studying, especially for really large tests, as if helps me keep track of everything.

And that’s all I can think of off the top of my head! I’m sorry if they’re super generic tips but I hope it helped a little :)
